title: Order Compatibility in Multi-View Linear Gaussian Models with Partially Paired Views
banked_reason: Final D0.5 math review passed, but the general referee assessed subfield (7.4) and the decision panel found the promised duplicate-free output-sensitive coefficient-tuple enumeration undelivered.
gap_reasons: The 2^p-state DAG enumerates compatible orders only; it does not deliver the promised output-sensitive, exact-once enumeration of distinct coefficient tuples.
The established fiber lemma canonicalizes inducing orders only after a tuple is known; traversing all compatible paths can remain factorial even when N_out=1.
The paper is mathematically sound and substantially strengthened, but the original field-level computational kernel remains unproved.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved a sound component-aligned Gaussian theory: fixed-order residual compatibility, arbitrary observation-graph positive-definite completion with chordal and nonchordal certificates, a generic one-pair calibration elbow, and graph-aware covariance-region and poset recovery. It could not turn the removed-set order DAG into a duplicate-free output-sensitive enumerator of distinct coefficient tuples; the needed child oracle would assume the unresolved crux and path traversal can remain factorial. A future re-raise needs a genuinely noncircular quotient algorithm or a precise hardness replacement, not another graph-completion or unrestricted-class extension.
tldr: On the restrictive component-aligned Gaussian LiMVAM class, a candidate common order is compatible with an arbitrary observed view graph exactly when every observed-edge residual cross-block is diagonal and every coordinatewise partial disturbance covariance admits a positive-definite completion. The signed completion value \(\chi_G\) makes this second condition computable and stable. A new arbitrary-graph covariance-region inversion combines one sourcewise-iid paired sample per observed edge with every view marginal, without requiring cross-source independence; away from explicit feasibility and path-product margins it gives confidence-set coverage, Hausdorff coefficient-set consistency, and exact graph-essential-poset recovery. The generic elbow still shows that one preassigned view pair generically identifies the full coefficient tuple, and the memoized removed-set recursion retains its \(2^p\)-state compatibility guarantee. Duplicate-free numerical tuple enumeration beyond compatible-order enumeration is not claimed.
gap: Heurtebise et al.'s Section 4.6, Assumption 2 and Theorem 3 give full-pair identification under edgewise correlation diversity on their broader disturbance class. DirectLiNGAM Section 3.1, Lemmas 1--2 and Corollary 1 justify recursive removal of one true exogenous variable. Shimizu's JointLiNGAM, Chen et al.'s individual-structure method, and Ghassami et al.'s multi-domain procedure borrow information across datasets or domains through non-Gaussianity, shared-population components, or shared structure with domain heterogeneity. None proves that an arbitrary pair fixed in advance attains full-calibration identification generically on a component-aligned Gaussian parameter space, locates every failure on a proper algebraic variety, or characterizes all surviving orders on that variety.
fill: The headline theorem clears the positive principal-minor denominators of every wrong-order residual restriction, proves nonvanishing by an explicit single-edge witness, and concludes that any preassigned view pair gives the full-view singleton outside a Lebesgue-null algebraic set. Supporting results supply fixed-order completion, complete path-independent recursion, equality-locus examples, a computational calibration certificate, and covariance-region inversion with explicit local stability moduli.
